chapter: Pittsburgh school days and old jealousies
title: Jealousy: the razor, the husband's girls and the wives who watched her
summary: Jealousy was mostly about women: a trumpeter's wife pulled a razor on her; a Tulsa woman wanted her dead; the Kirk wives quietly protected her.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Was there a lot of jealousy around then?
There was jealousy all during all my period. It was mostly around women. I remember once when I was with

Buzzin the Buzz and Harris show. We were traveling and it seems I was so tiny that - I said to you once before that one of the musicians grabbed me and threw me up in the air, just grabbed me and kissed me and kissed me. The reason I'm afraid of a knife, someone pulls a knife out I'll faint almost, because our trumpet player's wife happened to be around and when he did that, she pulled a razor out on me. I was nothing but a little girl. I became so frightened. Then her husband put me down and she hit me. I accidentally knocked her out because I was warding off her blows. That frightened me and I fainted.

One other time that I ran into something like that, my husband was very tall, handsome ladies' man and he was always teasing. He had one girl in Tulsa, Oklahoma, thinking that he was going to marry her, but his wife wouldn't allow it. I knew nothing about it and the wives were protecting me in the Andy Kirk band and I didn't know it. Bessie Lawson and Ophie Harrington and Mabel Durham and a couple of the girls, they lived across the street from me and when I got out to go to the store or anything I noticed they'd come out of the house and go to the store with me. He'd met one of the natives down there and she was very, very jealous of him. He was kidding around with her and she was trying to kill me. She was thinking that maybe I wouldn't give him a divorce to marry her. She was more in love with him than he was with her.
Did you ever run into her?

No, I never saw her. They said she was a blonde girl, something, I don't know. They described her to me but I never even went looking for her. I was so dumb, so full of music till they called me "Dummy". I never paid attention to any danger or anything else. There was always music around, but later on I discovered that the wives were protecting me and they often would protect me. There was quite a bit of jealousy around. With this Buz ZIN Harris thing, his wife was very jealous of me and one day he hit her in the eye. We happened to be out in the country and he walked around a cow all day because he said something like that if you put it on the eye it's like a raw steak. He was walking to get something to heal her eye.
